parsed.estimand: Additional deaths from a hurricane with a feminine rather than a masculine name, estimated as the difference in predicted deaths between the two name groups with the other predictors held at their sample means.

steps.title: Choose which storms to analyse
steps.description: Two storms account for most deaths; analysts differ on keeping them.

options.label: Drop the two deadliest storms
options.rationale: The original analysis set aside the two extreme-death storms.
options.spec: Remove the two rows with the highest alldeaths.

options.label: Keep every storm
options.rationale: Nothing in the question calls for discarding data.

options.label: Drop only the deadliest storm
options.rationale: A milder trim that removes the single most extreme observation.
options.spec: Remove the one row with the highest alldeaths.

options.label: Drop storms with more than 100 deaths
options.rationale: Critics of the original paper argued that very deadly storms should go.
options.source: Simonsohn, Simmons and Nelson (2020), Nature Human Behaviour 4

steps.title: Measure name femininity
steps.description: The data hold a coder rating, a second rating and a binary flag.

options.label: Coder rating (1 to 11)
options.rationale: A graded rating keeps the information in the names.

options.label: Female versus male name
options.rationale: The binary reading is the plain meaning of the claim.

options.label: Online-panel rating (1 to 11)
options.rationale: A second, independent set of raters scored the same names.

steps.title: Measure property damage
steps.description: Damage is heavily right-skewed and exists in two inflation bases.

options.label: Damage in 2015 dollars
options.rationale: Complete for every storm and on the scale analysts usually report.

options.label: Log of damage in 2015 dollars
options.rationale: A log scale tames the skew in damage.
options.source: Simonsohn, Simmons and Nelson (2020), Nature Human Behaviour 4

options.label: Damage in 2013 dollars
options.rationale: The measure used in the original paper.
options.spec: dam = ndam; storms with missing ndam drop out.

steps.title: Measure storm strength
steps.description: Three landfall measures describe the intensity of a storm.

options.label: Minimum pressure
options.rationale: Pressure at landfall is a direct physical measure of intensity.
options.spec: str = -min, so that a higher value means a stronger storm.

options.label: Maximum wind speed
options.rationale: Wind speed is the other common intensity measure.

options.label: Saffir-Simpson category
options.rationale: A standard five-level scale for storm strength.

steps.title: Choose the functional form for femininity
steps.description: Femininity can act on deaths alone or through damage and strength.

options.label: Interact with damage and strength
options.rationale: Femininity may matter more for damaging, intense storms.
options.spec: Include fem*dam, fem*str, fem*dam*str and dam*str.

options.label: Interact with damage only
options.rationale: A simpler interaction with the damage measure alone.

options.label: Main effect only
options.rationale: The most direct reading of the claim, with no interaction.

steps.title: Control for the era of the storm
steps.description: Reporting and preparedness changed over six decades.

options.label: No time control
options.rationale: The original analysis did not adjust for the year.

options.label: Year and year by damage
options.rationale: Allows deaths per unit of damage to drift over time.
options.source: Simonsohn, Simmons and Nelson (2020), Nature Human Behaviour 4

options.label: Post-1979 indicator and its interaction with damage
options.rationale: Names alternated between sexes from 1979, so era is entangled with name.
options.source: Simonsohn, Simmons and Nelson (2020), Nature Human Behaviour 4

steps.title: Fit the model
steps.description: Deaths are counts with a heavy right tail.

options.label: Negative binomial regression
options.rationale: Overdispersed counts call for a negative binomial model.
options.spec: NB2 log-link GLM, dispersion by maximum likelihood.

options.label: Linear model on log(deaths + 1)
options.rationale: A common alternative that is easy to inspect.
options.spec: OLS of ln(alldeaths + 1); effects back-transformed to deaths.
options.source: Simonsohn, Simmons and Nelson (2020), Nature Human Behaviour 4
